title: Bank Imaging Administrator
description:
Imaging Administrator Spire Leicester Oadby Bank Ad-Hoc Shifts Competitive Hourly Rate Weekly Pay

Spire Leicester Hospital are currently recruiting an Imaging Administrator to join their Admin department on a bank basis.

This is a flexible bank role, working on an "as and when required" basis to support staffing levels during busy periods and provide cover during periods of annual leave and absence.

The Role

As an Imaging Administrator, you'll provide essential administrative support to our multidisciplinary radiology team by:
- Managing and coordinating radiology appointments in line with departmental procedures.
- Contacting patients to arrange bookings and supporting them throughout their journey.
- Liaising with consultants, clinicians and hospital departments to ensure efficient service delivery.
- Processing radiology reports and ensuring timely distribution to the relevant recipients.
- Providing pricing information and estimates for self-pay patients.
- Maintaining accurate patient records across hospital and radiology information systems.
- Collecting, collating and reporting activity data, including NHS and BUPA reporting requirements.
- Supporting general departmental administration including filing, document management and correspondence.
- Ensuring compliance with data protection, confidentiality and information governance standards.
- Contributing to quality improvement initiatives and supporting the training and induction of new colleagues.

What We're Looking For
- Strong administrative and organisational skills.
- Excellent attention to detail with the ability to maintain accurate records.
- Good communication and interpersonal skills.
- Excellent keyboard and IT skills.
- The ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.

Benefits:

We offer employed colleagues a competitive salary as well as a comprehensive benefits package which includes but is not limited to:
- Bank colleagues are paid weekly
- We offer competitive rates to our bank colleagues who work on a flexible basis, often to cover busy periods, sickness, or annual leave
- Save an average of 50 per month with our free onsite car park
- Access to Spire Healthcare pension
- Access to Blue Light Card discounts
- Smartspending discounts (in addition to Blue Light discounts) via 'Spire for You'
- Wellbeing Centre access via 'Spire for You'
- Free uniform
- Free DBS
- Full induction, including mandatory training updates
- Opportunities for further training and progression into permanent posts
- Knowledge, support and guidance through your recruitment journey from Spire's specialist Resourcing Team

Our Values:

We are extremely proud of our heritage in private healthcare and of our values as an organisation:
- Driving clinical excellence
- Doing the right thing
- Caring is our passion.
- Keeping it simple
- Delivering on our promises
- Succeeding and celebrating together

We commit to our employees' well-being through work life balance, on-going development, support and reward.

Spire Healthcare is a leading independent healthcare group in the United Kingdom, running 38 hospitals and over 50 clinics across England, Wales and Scotland. It provides diagnostics, inpatient, day case and outpatient care, operates a network of private GPs and provides workplace health services to over 800 corporate clients. It also delivers a range of private and NHS mental health, musculoskeletal and dermatological services.

Spire Healthcare are proud to be an equal opportunities employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive culture for all. Our people are our difference, it's their dedication, warmth and pursuit of excellence that sets Spire Healthcare apart.

title: Office Administrator
description:
Here at C T Fire Protection, we re hiring an Office Administrator & Scheduling Assistant to join our team in South Kilworth, near Lutterworth.

You will work closely with our scheduling team, engineers and business managers, providing essential administrative and scheduling support to ensure our service, maintenance and installation teams are coordinated efficiently. This is a busy and varied role, ideal for someone who is organised, proactive and enjoys working in a fast-paced environment. This is a full-time role, but we would consider part-time hours for the right person.

What you receive for joining us:

We re offering a competitive salary based on experience, a permanent position with Monday Friday working hours, and the opportunity to develop your skills within an established and growing LPCB-certified fire protection company. You ll receive training and ongoing development, with the opportunity to progress within the business, working as part of a friendly and supportive team in a varied role within the fire protection industry. Additionally, you ll receive 25 days holiday per year plus Bank Holidays, your Birthday off and a company pension.

Here s a look at some of the things you ll be doing:
- Assist the Service Team Lead with scheduling and coordinating engineers and installation teams, organising service, maintenance and installation appointments, while managing daily diaries and updating schedules for field engineers
- Act as the first point of contact for incoming office calls and emails, maintaining a professional and friendly approach while providing a high level of customer service to customers and contractors
- Prepare documentation using Microsoft Office, update digital company systems and maintain accurate records for compliance purposes, including tracking quotes through online digital platforms and processing job sheets, timesheets and service reports
- Assist with invoicing and day-to-day administrative tasks for the management team, while acting as an operational systems champion to support compliance with internal QA systems and procedures and developing and maintaining the company s social media presence in line with Complii Group guidelines

Can you show experience in some of these areas:
- Are you highly organised with excellent attention to detail, able to manage multiple tasks, changing priorities and busy schedules while remaining calm and organised?
- Are you confident communicating with customers and contractors, with a professional, friendly and approachable manner and a strong commitment to customer service?
- Are you computer literate and confident using Microsoft Office and digital systems, with the ability to maintain accurate records and learn new systems quickly?
- Are you reliable, able to work independently and a good problem solver with a practical, proactive and can-do attitude?

Do you have previous experience in scheduling, administration, construction, engineering, facilities management or the fire protection industry? This would be advantageous but is not essential for the right candidate.

Introducing our organisation:

We are proud to be part of Complii. Complii is a leading integrated provider of safety and regulatory compliance services across our water, air, fire, electrical, and vertical transportation divisions, supporting organisations nationwide to operate safely, compliantly, and responsibly.

title: Sales Account Administrator
description:
Sales Account Administrator

Job Type: Permanent / Full-Time

Working Hours: Monday-Thursday, 8:15am-4:45pm; Friday, 8:00am-2:00pm

About the Role

We are looking for an organised, proactive and customer-focused Sales Account Administrator to join our team and provide essential administrative and commercial support to our sales function.

This is a varied role where you will act as a key point of contact for customers, helping to manage accounts, process orders, prepare quotations and ensure customers receive a high level of service throughout the sales process.

You will work closely with colleagues across Sales, Operations, Finance and Logistics, making this an excellent opportunity for someone who enjoys building relationships, solving problems and keeping things running smoothly.

Key Responsibilities

Customer & Account Management
- Act as the primary administrative contact for a portfolio of customer accounts.
- Build and maintain strong, professional customer relationships.
- Support the onboarding of new customers, including account setup and documentation.
- Respond promptly and professionally to customer enquiries relating to orders, pricing, lead times, deliveries and general account queries.
- Coordinate with internal teams to resolve customer concerns and technical queries.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date customer records, pricing, costings and contract information.

Sales Administration & Support
- Prepare quotations, proposals and sales documentation with a high level of accuracy.
- Process customer orders accurately and ensure they are entered into the ERP system in a timely manner.
- Monitor order progress and proactively communicate updates to customers.
- Assist with sales reports, forecasts and performance KPIs.
- Provide administrative support to sales management, including meeting preparation, presentations, diary/calendar management and follow-up actions.
- Help organise customer visits, external meetings and trade shows.

Finance & Operational Support
- Work closely with Finance to support invoicing and resolve invoice queries.
- Assist with credit checks and payment follow-up where required.
- Ensure the ERP system contains accurate and current product, pricing, delivery and customer information.
- Maintain a high level of accuracy when handling commercial and customer information.

Continuous Improvement
- Identify opportunities to improve sales administration and customer service processes.
- Support the introduction and implementation of effective processes and best practices.
- Take ownership of tasks and contribute positively to the wider team.

About You

We are looking for someone who is highly organised, commercially aware and confident communicating with customers and colleagues.

Essential Skills & Experience
- Previous experience in sales administration, account management, customer service or a similar customer-facing role.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities.
- Excellent attention to detail and a high level of accuracy.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel, Word and Outlook.
- Experience using an MRP or ERP system.
- Ability to work independently while also contributing effectively as part of a team.
- A customer-focused and professional approach.
- A proactive attitude with strong problem-solving skills.
- Ability to remain calm and effective when working under pressure.

Desirable
- Experience working within a fast-paced commercial or sales environment.
- Experience with sales reporting, forecasting or data analysis.
- Knowledge of manufacturing, engineering or another technical/commercial environment.

Personal Attributes

You will be:
- Customer-focused and service driven.
- Professional, confident and adaptable.
- Proactive and solutions focused.
- Highly organised and dependable.
- Comfortable taking ownership and accountability for your work.
- A positive team player who builds effective working relationships.
- Calm and professional when dealing with challenging situations.

What We Expect

You will be expected to handle customer and commercially sensitive information with the highest level of confidentiality and professionalism.

You will also be responsible for:
- Following company procedures and quality requirements.
- Maintaining high standards of accuracy and attention to detail.
- Working safely and taking responsibility for your own health and safety and that of colleagues.
- Using company equipment, systems and materials correctly and responsibly.
- Contributing ideas and suggestions that could improve processes, efficiency and customer service.

title: Casualty Claims Handler
description:
A renowned National Loss Adjusting Organisation are now seeking an experienced Liability Claims Handler to join their specialist Casualty Liability Team.
- You will handle a variety of specialist Liability claims on behalf of a number of Public Sector clients.
- You will manage and be responsible for your own caseload of losses, being part of a dedicated team you will play a vital part of the business by providing an exceptional claims service to key clients.
- Due to growth and expansion this will be an exciting time to join where you will be offered the opportunity to progress and develop long-term.

Key responsibilities:
- Handle a variety of casualty/personal injury claims through to settlement
- Verify policy cover/validity
- Log and record all claims digitally
- Investigate allocated claims either from desk or instructed by the team of loss adjusters
- Where appropriate refer to a field adjuster for site investigation to establish how the loss occurred
- Gather all necessary evidence and relevant documentation
- Determine appropriate action for resolution
- Make decision on liability and negotiate settlement where appropriate
- Keep up to date with any technical changes within the industry and to your role which may involve participating in training programmes within the company

About you:
- Liability/Casualty Claims handling experience working in the Loss Adjusting, Insurance or Legal Sector
- Experience of handling your caseload of claims through to settlement
- The ability to value an injury loss
- Experience of handling defendant losses
- The ability or understand insurance policy wordings and the insurance market
- Knowledge of civil procedure rules and the claims portal
- Excellent communication skills both verbal and written
- Good planning and organisational skills
- Solid IT skills and be able to use multiple in-house systems
- Insurance Industry Qualifications or working towards desirable

Benefits on Offer:
- Remote or hybrid depending on location, 35 hours per week Monday to Friday
- Flexible benefits including holiday purchase plan and the opportunity to purchase health cash and BUPA dental plan, flexible working, 5% pension, life assurance 4 x, enhanced maternity, paternity, and adoption pay, discounts with UK retailers, wellbeing hub and many more

title: Medical Receptionist
description: Medical Receptionist Vacancy. Broom Leys Surgery are seeking a friendly, professional and enthusiastic Medical Receptionist to join our busy and hard-working Patient Services Team. Please note that working patterns may also include 8:00 am starts and 6:30 pm finishes, so flexibility is essential. Benefits include: 5 weeks' annual leave plus Bank Holidays (pro rata) The option to join the NHS Pension Scheme On site parking We are looking for a candidate with excellent communications and interpersonal skills, strong customer service ethos and have the ability to multi-task. Experience in General Practice or SystmOne would be an advantage for this role, however full training will be given to the right candidate. The successful candidate will provide a range of duties such as: Project a positive, professional and welcoming image to patients and other visitors, both in person and on the telephone. Processing telephone requests for appointments, visits and telephone consultations and ensuring callers are directed to the appropriate healthcare professional. Completing tasks relating to patients and communicating with them in an efficient way Adding patient correspondence onto the clinical system and coding data. Processing repeat prescriptions in accordance with practice guidelines. Support the practice QOF and Enhanced Services. Job summary: The purpose of the role is to: Project a positive, professional and welcoming image to patients and other visitors, either in person or on the telephone Offer general assistance to the practice team and project a professional, positive and friendly image to patients and other visitors, either in person or via the telephone. Receive, assist and direct patients in accessing the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous, efficient and effective way. Undertake a variety of Patient Services Team duties to assist in the smooth running of the practice, support the clinical staff and other members of the practice team. Facilitate effective communication between patients, members of the primary health care team, secondary care and other associated healthcare agencies. Maintain patient confidentiality and adhere to Data Protection policies. Duties and responsibilities: The duties and responsibilities to be undertaken by members of the Patient Services Team may include any or all of the items in the following list. Duties may be varied from time to time under the direction of the Practice Manager, dependent on current and evolving practice workload and staffing levels: Maintaining and monitoring the practice appointments system. Receive, assist and direct patients to the appropriate service or healthcare professional in a courteous and practical way Processing incoming correspondence Computer data entry, processing and recording information in accordance with practice procedures. Filing and retrieving medical records. Initiating contact with and responding to requests from patients, other team members and associated healthcare agencies and providers. Providing clerical assistance to practice staff as required. Keeping the reception area, notice-boards and leaflet dispensers tidy and free from obstructions and clutter. Act as a chaperone if requested. Adhere to the information governance requirements of the NHS at all times To carry out ad-hoc duties as requested. This list of duties is not intended to be exhaustive, but indicates the main areas of work and may be subject to change after consultation with the post-holder to meet the changing needs of the Practice.
